import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Coefficient of $(xyz)^n$ in $((x+y)(y+z)(z+x))^n$ equaling $\binom{2n}{n}^3$

The sequence $a(n)$ is defined by $a(n) = \binom{2n}{n}^3$.

*References:*
- [A002897](https://oeis.org/A002897)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

namespace OeisA2897


open Polynomial

open Nat MvPolynomial

/--
The sequence $a(n)$ is defined by $a(n) = \binom{2n}{n}^3$.
We use `Nat.choose (2 * n) n` for the central binomial coefficient.
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ := (Nat.choose (2 * n) n) ^ 3

abbrev Vars := Fin 3

/--
The finsupp corresponding to the monomial $x^n y^n z^n$.
This is the map $\lambda i. n$. Since `Fin 3` is finite, this function is finitely supported.
-/
noncomputable def xyzPowN (n : ℕ) : Finsupp Vars ℕ :=
  Finsupp.ofSupportFinite (fun _ : Vars => n) (Set.toFinite _)

local notation "P" => MvPolynomial Vars ℤ

/--
The polynomial $pPoly(X, Y, Z) = (1 + X + Y + Z)^{2n} (1 + X + Y - Z)^n (1 + X - Y + Z)^n$.
We identify $X_0, X_1, X_2$ with $X, Y, Z$.
-/
noncomputable def pPoly (n : ℕ) : P :=
  let X := MvPolynomial.X 0
  let Y := MvPolynomial.X 1
  let Z := MvPolynomial.X 2
  let p1 : P := 1 + X + Y + Z
  let p2 : P := 1 + X + Y - Z
  let p3 : P := 1 + X - Y + Z
  p1 ^ (2 * n) * p2 ^ n * p3 ^ n


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 8 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 216 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 8000 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 343000 := by rfl


/--
Conjecture: $a(n) = [x^n y^n z^n] (1+x+y+z)^{2n} (1+x+y-z)^n (1+x-y+z)^n$. - _Peter Bala_, Apr 10 2022

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/2897.wip.lean#L408"]
theorem a_eq_coeff (n : ℕ) : (a n : ℤ) = MvPolynomial.coeff (xyzPowN n) (pPoly n) := by
    sorry

end OeisA2897

findings.description: The module title at line 20 claims that [(xyz)^n]((x+y)(y+z)(z+x))^n equals binomial(2n,n)^3. This is a different, false identity: at n=1 its coefficient is 2, whereas binomial(2,1)^3=8. By contrast, pPoly and a_eq_coeff correctly use (1+x+y+z)^(2n)(1+x+y-z)^n(1+x-y+z)^n. The error is confined to the mathematical title; the Lean declarations are faithful. The n=1 discrepancy was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without sorry.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A002897, Peter Bala's Apr 10 2022 comment, explicitly gives a(n) = [(xyz)^n](1+x+y+z)^(2n)(1+x+y-z)^n(1+x-y+z)^n. Read via https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A002/A002897.seq. Easwar, arXiv:2608.22053v2, Corollary 4.5, states exactly this identity for n≥0.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the title with “A coefficient identity for cubed central binomial coefficients”, or replace its polynomial with (1+x+y+z)^(2n)(1+x+y-z)^n(1+x-y+z)^n. Leave pPoly and a_eq_coeff unchanged.

reformulations.difference: Relative to the leading rational-function diagonal conjecture in Bala's April 2022 comment, the theorem uses the three-variable polynomial-coefficient form, which OEIS also explicitly supplies in the next sentence.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Homogenize the polynomial by replacing 1 with a fourth variable u. The resulting product H=(u+x+y+z)^(2n)(u+x+y-z)^n(u+x-y+z)^n is homogeneous of degree 4n. Consequently [x^n y^n z^n]H(1,x,y,z)=[u^n x^n y^n z^n]H. MacMahon's master theorem, applied to the matrix M in the OEIS comment, identifies this with the diagonal coefficient of 1/(1-(u+x)(1-4yz)-y-z), a renaming of Bala's rational function. Equality for every n is therefore equivalent to the generating-function diagonal identity. Easwar §4 gives this homogenization/MacMahon argument.

review.notes: All four definitions/abbreviations and all six lemma/theorem statements were checked; no declaration-level misformalization was found. Sequence evaluation matched OEIS for n=0..8; an independent exact coefficient routine matched its b-file for n=0..12. The research solved tag agrees with OEIS's May 31 2026 proof notice and Easwar's later independent proof. The exact archived formal-proof statement matches up to helper renaming and contains no admissions or custom axioms; its historical toolchain was not rebuilt.
